And it wasn't only those two — three of the top four were rookies (Damian 1st, Douang 2nd, Tony 4th), with the founders salvaging only Mikey in 3rd.

2012.title: 🔄 Churn Didn't Pay
2012.body: 2012 was the league's first big year on the waiver wire — and proof it doesn't buy a title. The two busiest managers worked the wire hardest and finished 3rd and 9th, while champion Damian barely touched it. The frantic activity mostly just funded the pot.

2012.title: 💀 Lam's Perfect One-Week Career
2012.body: Rookie Lam finished dead last (10th, 1,898) and was gone after one season — but his lone Week 14 explosion (153) was the week's High Man crown. One season, one HMOTW, then vanished. Honestly, a perfect TNCFL career.

2012.title: 👑 Coronation by the Numbers
2012.body: The rookie king's line: 2,451 points, 144.2 per week vs the league's 125.7, a 198-point margin, and a +$999 payday — the fattest check in the room. (2011's whole title was decided by 28.)

2012.title: 📉 The Champ's 71-Point Floor
2012.body: Hero to zero in one year: defending champ Hanh crashed from 1st to 9th (1,940), bottoming out with back-to-back 71s in Weeks 12 and 13 — the two lowest scores of the season.

2012.title: 🔁 214 Moves
2012.body: The wire ran hot in year two: 214 transactions added +$428 to the pot at $2 a move — yet champ Damian made just 15.

2012.title: 💣 Twin 197s
2012.body: Season's two biggest games, tied to the point: Damian (Wk5) and Douang (Wk8) both hit 197.

2012.title: 🔁 First Tracking Year
2012.body: 2012 was the first season the league formally tracked HMOTW crowns and drought streaks — the obsession this whole hub memorializes.

2013.title: 📉 The 444-Point Freefall
2013.body: The league devours its champions, and 2013 made the lesson brutal: defending champ Damian crashed from 1st (2,451) all the way to dead last, 10th of 10 at 2,007 — a 444-point collapse in twelve months, bottoming out with the season's lowest game (75 in Week 11) and a -$326 ledger. The man who lapped the field as a rookie ate its dust the very next year.

2013.title: 👰 The Eternal Bridesmaid
2013.body: Douang finished runner-up for the second straight year (2,597, after 2nd in 2012) — and for the second straight year he tied for the most HMOTW crowns in the league (5.0, including a three-week tear in Weeks 11–13 when he seized the standings lead). More weekly wins than the champion, again. Always the prettiest dress in the room, never the one at the altar.

2013.title: 💥 256 — in a Year of Empty 200s
2013.body: Kevin's 256 in Week 15 is the season high and the all-time league record that still stands. The wild context: it was one of seven 200+ games in 2013 — and every one paid like an ordinary win. The DHMOTW doubler was still three years away (2016), so the biggest scoring barrage in early league history earned nobody a dime extra.

2013.title: 🔄 Churn Didn't Pay (Again)
2013.body: Champion Kevin made just 12 moves, tied for the fewest in the league, while the two busiest — Hanh (42) and Mikey (39) — finished 9th and 3rd. The wire stayed busy; the title went to one of its quietest users.

2013.title: 🔁 257 Moves
2013.body: The wire ran hot: 257 transactions added +$514 to the pot — yet champ Kevin made just 12.

2013.title: 🎯 Won by 89
2013.body: Kevin edged runner-up Douang by just 89 points (2,686–2,597) — the title's full margin.

2013.title: 🏰 Five Kings
2013.body: Five managers led the standings over 8 lead changes.

2014.title: 🪆 The Voodoo Doll That Failed
2014.body: La's half-joking hex for the league leader had exactly one target all season — and it backfired completely. Rookie Randy grabbed first in Week 2, locked it for good in Week 4, and led 14 straight weeks to the title at 2,761 points, a league-best 162.4 per week (the field averaged 137.1) and a crushing 208-point margin. The third rookie in three years to walk in and steal the crown — and every voodoo pin only seemed to make him stronger. We were poking the man who'd go on to become the league's biggest all-time money earner.

2014.title: 🪙 Seven Different Crowns
2014.body: Randy ran away with the standings, but the weekly High Man crown wouldn't pick a king: seven different managers won a week in 2014. Randy led with just 5, then Mikey (4), Daniel and La (3 each), and single crowns for Damian, Hanh, and Tony. The title was decided early — the weekly glory was anyone's.

2014.title: 💀 The Crown Is a Target
2014.body: 2014 confirmed the league's central law: three straight defending champions dragged toward the cellar. Hanh fell to 9th in 2012, Damian to 10th in 2013, and now reigning champ Kevin collapsed to 9th (2,000), below the league average. The crown isn't a reward — it's a target painted on your back.

2014.title: 🕳️ Kito’s Double Bottom
2014.body: While the rain-dance card tells the drought tale, the standings told the rest: Kito finished dead last (10th, 1,988) and swallowed a season-worst -$349 — the same year his HMOTW drought stretched to a then-league-record 45 weeks. He bottomed out with a 73-point Week 17, the third-lowest score of the entire season — a fitting final whimper to a year with no crowns, no money, and no rain. And the cruelest part: it would get worse before it got better, the drought running eight more weeks into 2015 before it finally broke at 53.

2014.title: 🥊 The Pack Behind Randy
2014.body: While Randy ran off by 208, the fight for 2nd was a knife fight: La (2,553), Mikey (2,525), and Daniel (2,481) — three men separated by just 72 points.

2014.title: 🥉 Bronze 4-Peat
2014.body: Mikey: 3rd in 2011, 2012, 2013, and 2014 — the only manager to reach the podium in each of the league's first four seasons, and never once the top step. In 2014 he churned the wire harder than anyone (a league-high 61 moves) and still landed in the exact same spot. Mr. Consistency, perpetually one chair short.

2014.title: 💥 Randy’s 216
2014.body: Season high: Randy, 216 in Week 8 — at the time the 3rd-highest single week in league history, behind only Kevin's 256 and Douang's 217. And he dropped it while already leading the standings: not a climb, just a rookie champ stomping on the gas with the race long since his.

2014.title: 🔁 256 Moves
2014.body: 256 transactions, +$512 to the pot — and for all that frantic wheeling, champ Randy barely touched the wire. Money well spent, gentlemen.

2015.title: 🥉➡️👑 Bronze, Bronze, Bronze, Bronze… Gold
2015.body: The most patient breakthrough in league history: after four straight 3rd-place finishes (2011–2014), Mikey finally abandoned the bronze step and climbed to the top, winning his first title at 2,580 points on a career-best 151.8/week (field: 140.3). It was the first championship by a founding member since Hanh in 2011, snapping a three-year newcomer streak (Damian, Kevin, Randy). The man who couldn't escape third suddenly couldn't be caught.

2015.title: 💵 The Money Era Begins
2015.body: 2015 rewrote the economics: the buy-in doubled to $200, the league added a $250 championship ring voucher, and the payout expanded to four paid places (40/30/20/10) on a $2,288 pot. Mikey's title was the first to come with a ring — a $1,165.20 haul — and the brand-new 4th-place check landed in the most poetic hands imaginable: Kito's, the same year he finally broke his record drought.

2015.title: 🌧️ Rain at Last — and a Payday
2015.body: Kito broke his league-record 45-week drought, won 3 HMOTWs, and rode the resurrection to 4th place — which, thanks to the brand-new 4th-place payout, meant his first paycheck in years (+$93.80). The rain dance finally worked, and the timing couldn't have been better.

2015.title: 💀 Four Champs, Four Cellars
2015.body: The crown's curse became undeniable: four straight defending champions buried. Hanh 9th (2012), Damian 10th (2013), Kevin 9th (2014), and now reigning champ Randy sank to 9th (2,165). Win here and the league marks you.

2015.title: 🧊 La’s 58
2015.body: Week 10: La scored 58 — the lowest week ever, still unbeaten.

2015.title: 🎯 Won by 43
2015.body: Mikey edged Tony by just 43 points — a wire fight.

2015.title: 🔁 259 Moves
2015.body: A busy wire: 259 transactions league-wide added +$518 to the pot at $2 a move.

2015.title: 🏃 Busiest Won
2015.body: Champion Mikey was the most active manager (47 moves).

2016.title: 🪦 The Lazarus Line
2016.body: No one else has this résumé: Damian's career path reads 1st → 10th → 5th → 7th → 1st. Champion as a 2012 rookie, dead last in 2013, two quiet years in the wilderness — then in 2016 he surged into first in Week 9 and never let go, reclaiming the crown at 2,624 points (154.4/wk vs the league's 139.9). The only man in league history to win it, crash to the cellar, and rise to win it all again.

2016.title: 💥 The DHMOTW Era Opens
2016.body: 2016 introduced the Double High Man: crack 200 in a week and the weekly pot doubles — funded by bumping the weekly premium from $10 to $20. Fittingly, the league's first two DHMOTWs ever were both Damian's, back-to-back (205 in Week 9, 200 in Week 10) at the exact moment he seized the lead. The doublers pushed the season's HMOTW tally to 19.0 — 17 weeks plus two bonus crowns.

2016.title: 🏎️ Second by a Rounding Error
2016.body: The tightest podium ever: Kevin (2,555) edged Randy (2,544) for 2nd by just 11 points, while Damian's margin for 1st was 69. Both ran championship-caliber seasons; both watched a resurrected man hoist the trophy. Eleven points they'll replay for years.

2016.title: 💀 Five Champs, Five Cellars
2016.body: The crown's curse went a perfect 5-for-5: defending champ Mikey collapsed from 1st to 7th, joining Hanh, Damian, Kevin and Randy. Five straight title-holders dragged down the very next season — a law as dependable as gravity.

2016.title: 🌵 Tony in the Sand
2016.body: 2015's breakout runner-up went 23 weeks dry — new desert king.

2016.title: 🏜️ Kito Back to Last
2016.body: A year after escaping, Kito fell to dead last (2,117), -$450.

2016.title: 🤝 Week 17 Tie
2016.body: Damian & Douang tied at 163 — split crown.

2016.title: 🔁 248 Moves
2016.body: 248 transactions league-wide added +$496 to the pot — champ Damian made just 17.

2017.title: 👑 The Narrator Comes Home
2017.body: Six years after the founding title, the man telling these stories finally wrote himself a happy ending. After a wilderness run of 9th, 9th, 7th, 8th, 8th, Hanh stormed back to win 2017 at 2,491 points on a league-best 5 weekly crowns and a 146.5 average (vs 134.7), seizing first for good in Week 16. It was his second championship — and his first actual ring, since the 2011 founding crown predated ring vouchers (which began in 2015). The historian became the headline.

2017.title: 💵 The WTA Side Bet Arrives
2017.body: 2017 debuted a brand-new way to lose money: the Winner-Take-All side bet. Throw in an extra $100, and whoever among the entrants scores the most points by season's end takes the whole pot. Seven brave souls anted up for a $700 pool — and the man having his career-best season scooped it: Hanh, the top scorer of all seven entrants, folded the $700 into a season haul of +$1,827, one of the fattest in league history.

2017.title: 🔗 The Curse Finally Blinks
2017.body: For five straight years a defending champion had collapsed the season after winning. In 2017 Damian broke it: the reigning 2016 champ backed up his title with a 2nd-place finish — the first time a titleholder ever followed a crown with another podium.

2017.title: 🏎️ Three Points for Second
2017.body: The tightest podium gap yet: Hanh held the field off by 54, but behind him Damian (2,437) edged Mikey (2,434) for 2nd by just 3 points — the 2015 champ a hair short of silver, his specialty.

2017.title: 🏆 Both Podiums, Both 1sts
2017.body: Hanh's running joke, confirmed: his only two top-3 finishes (2011, 2017) are both titles.

2017.title: 🏜️ Randy in the Sand
2017.body: The 2014 rookie champ closed on a 26-week drought — the league's longest active.

2017.title: 🧊 Kevin’s 65
2017.body: Bound for last, Kevin bottomed out at 65 in Week 9.

2017.title: 🔁 283 Moves
2017.body: A busy wire: 283 transactions, +$566 to the pot.

2018.title: 🏜️➡️👑 From Driest to King
2018.body: The fastest desert-to-crown turn in league history: just a year after ruling the Sa-RANDY Desert on a 26-week drought as the league's driest man, Randy stormed to his second title (after 2014) at 2,793 points on a monstrous 164.3 average (league: 146.5). He grabbed the lead for good in Week 10 and never flinched. From punchline to champion in twelve months — the most complete reinvention since Damian rose from the dead.

2018.title: 💥 The DHMOTW Barrage
2018.body: 2018 turned the Double High Man rule into a fireworks show: six weeks saw a winner crack 200 and bank a doubled pot — Mikey (206, Wk1), Randy (205, Wk2), Damian (209, Wk4), Kito (210, Wk7), Kevin (207, Wk10) and Damian again (202, Wk14). Three years earlier the rule debuted with just two such weeks; 2018 tripled it and pushed the season's HMOTW tally to 23.0 — 17 weekly crowns plus six bonus doublers. The arms race had officially arrived.

2018.title: 📈 The Wettest Season Yet
2018.body: 2018 was the highest-scoring season in league history — a 146.5 weekly average, topping 2013's old high of 140.7 — with five managers clearing 2,500 points (Randy, Mikey, La, Kevin, Damian). The points poured down on everyone.

2018.title: 🥈 Silver Again
2018.body: Mikey posted a monster 2,747 and tied for the league lead with 5 weekly crowns — and still finished 46 points short in 2nd. The 2015 champ keeps collecting near-misses the way other men collect rings.

2018.title: 💣 The Triple-200 Week
2018.body: Week 4 had three men clear 200 (Damian 209, Mikey 206, Douang 200) — only the high man doubled.

2018.title: 🏆 Kito’s 210
2018.body: Single biggest game of the year: Kito, 210 (Week 7).

2018.title: 📉 Curse Returns
2018.body: Defending champ Hanh slid to 8th — the throne bites again.

2018.title: 🔁 271 Moves
2018.body: 271 transactions league-wide added +$542 to the pot.

2019.title: 👑 The Fewest-Crowns Champion Ever
2019.body: No champion ever won the title doing less of the winning. Kito took 2019 at 2,648 points (league-best 155.8 avg vs 145.0) while claiming a weekly High Man crown exactly once all year — his lone 205 in Week 15 — the fewest weekly wins by any champ in league history. He simply parked in 2nd or 3rd for sixteen weeks and pounced. The symmetry is perfect: eight years after Hanh stole the 2011 title from him with a Week 16 overtaking, Kito won this one by overtaking Randy in Week 16.

2019.title: 🏎️ Fifteen Weeks, No Ring
2019.body: Randy didn't lead 2019 so much as own it: five of the first seven weekly crowns (a Wk1–3 three-peat plus 5 and 7), a season-best 216 in Week 5, and fifteen unbroken weeks in first. He averaged a frankly unfair 168.8 through Week 9 before cooling. Then Kito caught him in Week 16 and he finished 2nd by 50 — the best manager in the field by every weekly measure, and still no ring.

2019.title: 🏜️ The 96-Week Record, Buried by Its Owner
2019.body: Bao — the two-smoke-pick founder, back after a five-year absence (last seen 2013) — walked in and in his fourth game back (Week 4) ended a 96-week drought, the longest in league history. The streak had climbed all through his exile (76 weeks by 2017, 93 by 2018) before he buried his own record at last.

2019.title: 💸 The Loser Cashed Biggest
2019.body: 2019's cruelest math: the man who lost the title walked out the league's richest. Randy added the $700 Winner-Take-All sweep (7 entrants, top scorer wins) to his 2nd-place money for +$1,427.90 — dwarfing champion Kito's +$885.20. Everything but the ring.

2019.title: 🧟 La’s 9-Point Bronze
2019.body: Stuck 8th–10th from Wk5–15, then a 206 in Wk16 vaulted La to 3rd — edging Damian by 9.

2019.title: 🆕 Ted’s Bipolar Debut
2019.body: Rookie Ted posted the season-low 75 (Wk4) and a 200 DHMOTW (Wk8) — then got bumped from the money at the final gun.

2019.title: 💦 Tony’s 758 Days
2019.body: Tony's 193 in Wk9 snapped a 38-week drought — 758 calendar days — the second desert to fall in 2019.

2020.title: 👑 THE PERFECT SEASON, Wire to Wire — and a Second Ring
2020.body: Hanh grabbed first in Week 1 and never let go, leading all 17 weeks — the first gate-to-tape title in league history and the longest single-season reign at #1, breaking Randy's 2019 record of 15. The 2,710-point run was his third championship (2011, 2017, 2020) and, in the voucher era of all-different champions, made him the first manager to earn two rings.

2020.title: 🔥 Two Biggest Games — and Still Silver
2020.body: Reigning champ Kito spent 2020 on a one-man barrage: a 215 in Week 14, then a 222 in Week 16 — at the time the second-highest single week in league history, behind only Kevin's all-time 256 from 2013. The two biggest games of the season were both his, and he tied for the league lead with 5 weekly crowns. And, most Kito of all, he still lost — taking 2nd by 28. The man drops the year's two biggest games and pockets the silver.

2020.title: 🆕 The Rookie Who Nearly Did It
2020.body: "Dilly Dilly" — rookie D'lyn — surged from 6th into the money, claimed 2nd by Week 12, and held it five weeks with the crown in sight. A benched QB in the final game cost him both placements: he finished 3rd, just 2 points behind Kito for silver and 30 behind Hanh for the ring.

2020.title: 🦠 The Record-Money Pandemic Season
2020.body: A captive audience refreshing the waiver wire all year drove a record 429 transactions — 140 past the old high. The league also ran its first-ever playoff (Mikey beat Kevin in the inaugural Superbowl, $350 to $100) and a $1,000 Winner-Take-All with all ten managers in. Hanh swept the WTA too, for a record +$2,098.20 payday.

2020.title: 🎆 Seven DHMOTWs
2020.body: A record 7 doubled weeks — Hanh ×2, Mikey ×2, Kito ×2, La — topping the old high of six set in 2018.

2020.title: 🏈 The First Playoff
2020.body: 2020 bolted on a bracket — Mikey edged Kevin in the first Superbowl on a flex tiebreaker.

2020.title: 🌦️ Randy: First to Driest
2020.body: A year after 15 weeks in first, Randy went last in earnings (-$667) and 27 weeks dry.

2020.title: 📉 Damian’s Freefall
2020.body: Reigning 2016-era contender Damian crashed to last (2,011) with the season-low 72 (Wk10).

2021.title: 👑 The Rookie Wrecking Ball
2021.body: The league's recurring nightmare got a new name: Titi, a rookie, who didn't just win in his first season — he obliterated it. He grabbed first in Week 3, locked it for good in Week 5, and led 15 of 18 weeks (the final 14 unbroken) to a 2,978.7-point title — the highest-scoring championship in league history, by both total and per-week (165.5). His 158.6-point margin was the most lopsided since Damian's 2012 rookie blowout, and his 6 weekly crowns led the field. The veterans circled the kid all year and never landed a glove.

2021.title: 🔥 Champion to Cellar, the Hard Way
2021.body: The defending-champ curse at its cruelest. Kito — 2019 champion, 2020 silver, owner of a 222-point game — came back in 2021 and finished dead last (2,507.8). The twist: he opened with the season's biggest game, a 235.5 in Week 1 (2nd-highest ever, behind only Kevin's 256), then never won another week all year, sliding straight to 10th. From a scoring record to the basement in seven days. His weekly rank told the whole story: 1st after Week 1, 10th by Week 16, three consecutive weeks in last to close out the season. Final net: −$444.

2021.title: 💪 Randy’s Redemption
2021.body: A year removed from the drought crown and last-place earnings, Randy stormed to 2nd (2,820.1), won three weekly crowns, broke his own drought, and banked +$1,162.30. From driest man in the league to runner-up in twelve months.

2021.title: 🆕 The 18-Week Era Opens
2021.body: 2021 expanded to an 18-week regular season — the first ever longer than 17 — as decade-long mainstays La and Mikey stepped away. Two rookies took their chairs: Titi, who walked to the throne, and Tim, who walked into the desert. The biggest roster turnover since the 2012 expansion.

2021.title: 🏆 Two of the Top 3 Ever
2021.body: 2021 alone produced the #2 and #3 weeks in history: Kito's 235.5 and Titi's 224.6.

2021.title: 🎆 Six DHMOTWs
2021.body: Six doubled weeks — five of them in the first six weeks, a front-loaded barrage.

2021.title: 🗡️ The Middle Knife-Fight
2021.body: 3rd through 5th — Tony, Kevin, Ted — finished within 44.5 points, with Tony grabbing the last podium spot and Ted just missing the money.

2021.title: 🏜️ Tim’s Winless Welcome
2021.body: The other rookie went his whole 18-week debut without a crown — 9th, 18 weeks dry.

2022.title: 🚧 Block the Titi Tyrant
2022.body: Titi's rise is getting absurd. It's only his 2nd season and he's already buried Ted (5.0 career HMOTW, 4th year) and D'lyn (3.0, 3rd year) — Titi sits at 13.0. Next in his sights is Tony, the 11-year veteran at 17.5, and Titi is already 74% of the way there. Someone needs to cut in front of this kid and slow him down — he's making every veteran look bad and walking off with all our money.

2022.title: 🔄 257 Moves
2022.body: The league churned 257 transactions at $2 a pop — pumping +$514 into the pot, nearly a quarter of the final $2,282 purse. The wire was busiest: Titi (40) and Randy (39) led the churn; Damian (7) barely touched it.

2022.title: 🏝️ Kito's Monday-Night Miracle
2022.body: Week 5 came down to the wire on Monday. Tony sat on 204.28 with his night done; Kito — watching from a beach in Hawaii — was near the bottom after Sunday with four players still to play. Then Mahomes and Jacobs closed the gap, Carlson and Adams out-burned the rest, and Kito roared past for 217.22 and a doubled pot — catapulting from 7th place to 2nd. It ended a 21-week desert drought dating to his monster 235.48 in Week 1 of last year. Two lunch coupons, well earned.

2022.title: 👑 Co-Crown, No Argument
2022.body: Kito and Titi both finished at 7.0 HMOTW tally — a dead-heat for the weekly crown. No one else was close; Tony was 3rd at 5.0. Kito won it from a beach in Hawaii; Titi won it while dismantling veterans twice his tenure.

2022.title: 🐸 The Pond-Scum Standings
2022.body: After Week 3 we finally got our answer from last week: yes, Damian climbed out of the cellar. But 9th place is less “escape” and more the fungus that feeds on the pond scum — because only one man sits lower, and it's Tim, the pus that infects the mucous that cruds up the fungus that feeds on the pond scum. (Yes — a My Best Friend's Wedding quote deployed as a fantasy-football analogy. Takes a bow. Thank you.) Tim flashed a glimmer of stepping into the sunlight to start the year, but Shrek dragged him back into the swamp. Best of luck, Tim — we're all rooting for that first crown.

2022.title: 🏇 The Front-Runner
2022.body: Tony led the standings 16 of 18 weeks (88.9%) and became just the 2nd champ in league history to sit in first after Week 1 — joining Hanh's 2020 wire-to-wire run. He won on grind: a 165.1 weekly average and no blowups, not a single explosion.

2022.title: 🏈 Bridesmaid in the Bracket
2022.body: Regular-season champ, playoff bridesmaid — again. For the 2nd straight year Tony reached the playoff Superbowl and lost, this time to Randy, who turned a 5th-place finish into the $400 bracket title. In 2021 it was Titi who denied him; the league crown still won't come with a playoff ring.

2023.title: 🏆 Tim’s Complete Game
2023.body:
Two winless seasons, then a sweep. Tim led the standings 10 of 18 weeks (9 straight to close the season), won the HMOTW race at 7.0 tally including back-to-back DHMOTWs (Wk 12 209.64, Wk 15 203.70), and topped every pool he entered: $944 prize + $250 ring + $700 HMOTW + $1,000 sidebet = +$2,232 net, 2nd-largest single-season haul in league history.

Season avg: 160.7 pts/wk, highest in the league. His 39-week drought (dating to career debut) ended Wk 4 on a 182.26 — his first-ever HMOTW crown. He never fell below 2nd place in the standings after that.

2023.title: 🔄 275 Moves
2023.body: 275 transactions at $2 + 30 trades at $2/player pumped +$610 into the pot. Busiest: Titi (45 moves). Most efficient: Damian (7 moves) — fewest in the league, still finished 3rd place.

2023.title: 📸 Wk 13: 1.16-Point Clump
2023.body: Tightest HMOTW race of the season. Damian won with 175.06, edging Kevin (174.70) by 0.36 pts. Ted (174.36) and Tim (173.90) were right behind — the top 4 separated by just 1.16 points after 18 games.

2023.title: 💥 Wk 16: The Chaos Week
2023.body: Randy dropped 225.64 — the 5th-highest single-week score in league history, behind Kevin’s 256 (2013), Kito’s 235 (2021), Damian’s 233 (2024), and Tim’s 231 (2025). Titi scored 65.12 the same week. The spread: 160.52 points, widest of the season.

2023.title: 🎲 Randy: Feast or Famine
2023.body: League-high variance: std dev 36.8. Season floor: 67.14 (Wk 1). Season ceiling: 225.64 (Wk 16). Also spent 10 of 18 weeks in last place in the cumulative standings — yet rallied to finish 7th overall.

2023.title: 🔥 Six DHMOTW Weeks
2023.body: Doubled-pot weeks (≥200): Kito Wk 3 (206.70), Ted Wk 5 (220.52), Damian Wk 8 (202.90), Tim Wk 12 (209.64), Tim Wk 15 (203.70), Randy Wk 16 (225.64). Six winners, six different weeks, $20 premium per crown. Defending champ Tony: 0.0 tally all season.

2023.title: 💃 D’lyn’s Last-Second Rain
2023.body: Carried the league’s longest active drought (39 weeks) into the final game of the regular season — then won it. Wk 18: 189.92, the weekly high, ending a streak tied for 4th-longest in league history alongside Tim and Douang. Also walked away with the playoff bracket crown ($400) that same postseason.

2024.title: 🏆 Randy By the Numbers
2024.body:
All-time single-season records, all set in 2024. 10.0 HMOTW tally — 3 crowns clear of the previous best (7.0); won 6 weeks (Wks 4, 5, 7, 15, 16, 17), four as DHMOTWs. Closed with 3 straight doubled pots: 215.58 → 203.44 → 221.54.

Season total: 3,104.20 pts. Avg: 172.5/wk. Floor: 138.36 (Wk 14) — his worst week still beat 7 other managers’ season averages. Led the standings 12 of 18 weeks.

Net: +$2,902 — league record. $908 prize + $250 ring + $1,000 HMOTW + $1,000 sidebet + $400 playoff.

2024.title: 💥 Nine DHMOTW Weeks
2024.body:
Prior record: 7 (2020). Three weeks had multiple managers over 200 — the doubled pot goes only to the weekly high each time.

Multi-200 collisions:
Wk 5 — Randy 204.36 over Tim 202.52 (gap: 1.84 pts)
Wk 11 — Damian 233.60 over D’lyn 202.18
Wk 15 — Randy 215.58 over Tony 204.42

Damian’s 233.60 = 3rd-highest single-week score all-time (Kevin 256 in 2013, Kito 235 in 2021).

2024.title: 💸 27.0 Tally → $270 Fee
2024.body: Nine DHMOTW weeks pushed the league-wide tally to 27.0, the highest in league history. Every manager paid the flat HMOTW fee of $270 — also a record. Managers who tallied zero (Kito) paid $270 and earned back nothing. Randy’s 10.0 tally earned $1,000 back at $10 × 10 managers per crown unit.

2024.title: 🏜 Kito’s Collapse
2024.body: 0.0 tally. 10th place (2,394.50). 11 of 18 weeks in last. Avg: 133.0/wk — lowest in the league. Drought: 33 weeks and counting.

2024.title: 🤜 4th–6th: 23 Points
2024.body: Tony (2,749.44), D’lyn (2,732.48), Ted (2,726.08) — three managers, 23.36 pts across 18 weeks. None made the money. All three netted between −$304 and −$458.

2024.title: 🌊 Hanh: Last Man Standing
2024.body: The only manager to seriously challenge Randy. Led standings in Wks 3, 9, 10, 14. Posted 5.0 HMOTW tally with DHMOTWs in Wk 9 (208.70) and Wk 14 (209.26). Finished 2nd at 2,956.04, avg 164.2/wk. Net: +$519 — the only other manager in the black.

2024.title: 🔄 253 Moves
2024.body: 253 trans ($2 ea.) + 7 trades ($2/player) = +$520 to pot. Busiest: Ted (42). Fewest: Damian (10) — still posted the season's biggest single game.

2024.title: 🥅 Closest Race: 1.84 pts
2024.body: Wk 5 — Randy 204.36 over Tim 202.52: a gap of 1.84 points, the tightest HMOTW finish of the season. Both cleared 200; only Randy got the doubled pot.

2025.title: 🏆 Aidan By the Numbers
2025.body:
1st place (2,909.04 pts). Led the standings 14 of 18 weeks (14 straight from Wk 5 to finish). HMOTW tally: 7.0 — league-high, including 3 DHMOTWs (Wk 5: 213.22 • Wk 7: 215.84 • Wk 12: 205.72).

Season avg: 161.6 pts/wk, highest in the league. Season high: 215.84 (Wk 7) — 5th-highest single-week score all-time. Net: +$2,183.20 — $903.20 prize + $250 ring + $700 HMOTW + $1,000 sidebet.

Year 1 (2024): 9th place. Year 2 (2025): 1st place, ring, every pool. Kevin (2nd, 2,749.38) and Damian (3rd, 2,740.72) finished within 9 points of each other but neither was ever close to first — Aidan led wire-to-wire from Week 5.

2025.title: 📊 The Leadership Race
2025.body: Tony led Wks 1–2, Hanh led Wks 3–4, then Aidan took over in Wk 5 and never looked back. Only 2 lead changes all season. Kevin held 2nd for most of the back half; Damian closed to within 8.66 pts for 3rd. Five managers finished within 100 points of each other in spots 4–8.

2025.title: 🔥 Five DHMOTW Weeks
2025.body: Wk 15 was the season’s flashpoint: Kito 210.32 over Hanh 209.00 by 1.32 points — both cleared 200, only Kito collected the doubled pot. Five total DHMOTW weeks; Aidan accounted for three of them. League tally: 23.0 → HMOTW fee $230/mgr.

2025.body: 250 trans ($2) + 4 trades ($2/player) = +$508 to pot. Busiest: Aidan (45), Ted (38). Fewest: Kevin (12) — finished 2nd.

2025.title: 🏜 Kito & Mikey
2025.body:
Kito broke a 33-week drought with a Wk 15 DHMOTW (210.32), rallied from 10th in 2024 to 5th (2,701.10). Drought now: 3 wks.
Inactive Mikey: 95 weeks — one shy of Bao’s all-time record of 96.
